content.comment_body: Hello, I'm entirely new to [product_name]. I have a setup with five weekly timers using logic gates that trigger five counters when a shared input is true. Timer 1 is configured for Monday to Friday, starting at 6 and stopping at 14; Timer 2 for Monday to Friday, from 14 to 22; Timer 3 for Monday to Thursday, from 22 to 6; Timers 4 and 5 for Saturday/Sunday only. However, during simulation with the internal clock running on a Saturday, both Timer 3 and the correct Timer 4 are active. Timer 3 stays active regardless of selected days. Any suggestions for resolving this?
Hi [user_name], could you share your circuit diagram? With it, we might be able to test and help you further. Best regards, [user_name]

Hello, If you'd like Weekly Timer 3 to operate overnight, you'll need two configurations. For example, to activate the timer on Monday from 22:00 to 6:00, set the ON time under configuration 1 for Monday and the OFF time under configuration 2 for Tuesday. Please refer to the attachment for timer B003 as an example. Also, in simulation mode, clicking the clock icon lets you easily verify if timers switch at the correct times.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing issues where weekly timers remain active on unintended days in simulation mode, likely due to improper setup for timers spanning midnight. Correct configuration requires attention to transitions between days and may involve using multiple timer settings. Feedback from simulation does not clearly indicate why a timer remains active longer than specified.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates each weekly timer will activate strictly according to specified days and time ranges—even when crossing midnight—and expects simulation results to directly mirror actual device behavior. Clear timer control and predictable simulation remain important for accurate programming.
